correctness.rationale: The fused map F(y)=1+(1−1/L)y=y+(L−y)/L, L=2^q, makes the p-bit stochastic-rounding chain nondecreasing on finitely many floats in [1,L]. With upward probability computed from downward p+r-bit truncation, upward motion is possible iff the increment crosses the p+r-grid quantum. Below L, final p-spacing Δ=2^(q−p), higher-grid spacing Δ/2^r. If r<q, the first absorbing state reachable from below is B=L−(2^(q−r)−1)Δ, and no state can jump over B; if r≥q the unique absorber is L. Positive upward probability at all preceding states and independent choices prove finite-time almost sure absorption; the last predecessor is visited and has exact geometric holding mean 2^r or 2^q. Ideal SR always reaches L. Independently enumerated 115 full exact rational reachable finite chains and final holding laws; infinite integer parameter proof is monotonic finite-chain/grid reasoning.
residual_risks: Normal arithmetic with wide exponent range, exact FMA, truncation-derived probabilities, independent random draws required; different rounding rules may have different thresholds.

value.rationale: Gives a sharp and counterintuitive limitation of finite-random-bit stochastic rounding under a fused operation: correct asymptotic limit iff r≥q and severe deterministic underestimation otherwise; quantifies exact waiting time. The natural geometric polynomial isolates a universal feedback saturation problem.
residual_risks: Limited to fixed geometric x=1−2^(−q), all-one coefficients, no finite-degree uniform error bound; not necessarily representative of other SR implementations.

limitations: p≥q+1, q≥2, r≥1, normal binary floating-point, exact fused multiply-add and p+r truncation in probability, independent choices, n→∞ with fixed p,q,r.
